subject: The 2AM mistake that changed everything
preview_text: I coded the no-contact tracker at 3AM after my own breakup spiral. Here's why.
body_paragraphs: Three months ago, I was lying on my bathroom floor at 2AM, crying so hard I couldn't breathe. My ex had just posted a photo with someone new, and I had broken no-contact for the 12th time. I texted my best friend, but she was asleep. So I did the only thing I could: I opened a blank code editor and started typing.

That night, I built the first version of our Emergency Mode. I needed something that would stop me from reaching out, from checking their profile, from falling back into the spiral. So I coded a button that would lock my phone for 10 minutes and play a recorded message from my past self: 'You deserve better. You've survived every bad day so far.' It wasn't pretty. But it worked.

That messy, raw 2AM code is now the core of our Emergency Mode feature. When you're in that 3AM spiral — heart racing, thumb hovering over their name — tap the red button. It gives you a 10-minute pause, a breathing exercise, and a note from someone who's been there. It's not magic. It's just a reminder that the urge passes. And you will too.

Open the app and try Emergency Mode right now. Even if you're not in a spiral, just see it. Know it's there for you when the floor drops. P.S. — I still use it sometimes. The code is ugly, but the relief is real.
